messages:
alan_cust: We're seeing a sharp p99 latency spike and some 502s on /v1/generate for ACME tenant starting ~2025-03-17T09:03Z. p95 went from ~200ms -> 1.2s, p99 ~9-12s. No customer-side change.

jess_support: Sorry about that — looking now. Can you DM the tenant id + a sample request id so we can pull logs? :eyes: 

alan_cust: Tenant: acme-42. Example request id: req_20250317_090312_abcd. Attached a snippet of the request headers (no sensitive data).

jess_support: Pulling logs... I see repeated allocator retries and GPU memory pressure around 09:02-09:05. Noted a pattern of large KV growth on the shard that serves acme-42. Pinging @marc_runtime and @kavita_oncall for runtime-side triage.

marc_runtime: Looking at runtime metrics now. Confirmed sustained GPU free-memory dips to single-digit MB on one node, plus many slow host-side allocations that line up with p99 tails. KV cache size for acme-42 grew ~3x in the window. Likely fragmentation + KV retention causing extra host->device latency and occasional 502s when allocator times out.

kavita_oncall: FWIW, the cluster shows increased host swap activity right after the KV spike. I'm ready to run mitigations. Immediate options: throttle tenant concurrency, trigger targeted KV eviction for tenant, or roll affected pods. Which do you want first?

jess_support: Quickest harm-reduction: 1) throttle tenant concurrency to 2 concurrent requests, 2) trigger targeted KV eviction, 3) route traffic to smaller model variant while we stabilize. Can we do those in sequence?

marc_runtime: Agreed. Commands I'll run:

```
# throttle concurrency
shardctl tenant_throttle --tenant acme-42 --concurrency 2

# targeted KV eviction (evict prefix used by conversation histories)
shardctl evict_kv --tenant acme-42 --prefix "conv:" --confirm
```

I'll also stage a fallback route to redwood-small-qa for acme-42 for 5m. That should cut KV footprint and token pressure.

ryan_infra: Starting targeted slab compaction on pool-7 (node n-7). ETA ~40s. Also increasing allocator retry backoff so we avoid busy-looping allocations.

deploy_bot: Canary routing change started: route acme-42 -> redwood-small-qa (10% of requests) (deploy id: dpl-20250317-07).

marc_runtime: After eviction + throttle + compaction we still saw a few long tails but p99 dropped from ~10s -> ~1.1s. 502s rate dropped by ~85%. Still seeing a handful of 502s tied to requests that hit a node pre-compaction.

alan_cust: Seeing big improvement on our side — p99 now ~1.1s and p95 ~320ms. Thanks. A few retries still fail but much better.

jess_support: Good to hear. We'll keep the throttle and fallback for a little while while we roll a permanent fix. Next steps for postmortem: gather full KV growth timeline, add tenant-level auto-throttle when KV growth crosses threshold, and consider allocator tuning to reduce fragmentation (alignments and slab compaction heuristics).

marc_runtime: Filing follow-up RFC to add: (a) automatic tenant backpressure based on KV delta, (b) background slab compaction that runs during low load windows, (c) a safety net to route tenants to model variants when device-free-memory < X MB. Also planning a small runtime change that reduces slab bucket sizes for long-running tenants to limit fragmentation.

kavita_oncall: Logging an incident ticket and scheduling a short post-incident runbook update. Will follow up with exact mitigation commands used and the timeline.

jess_support: Thanks everyone. @alan_cust we'll keep monitoring and will ping when the canary is fully rolled back to normal routing and allocator patch is deployed. :thumbsup:
